topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing and outlines the learning objectives for the cancer therapy lecture.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine foundational non-targeted cancer treatments, focusing on the mechanisms, applications, and systemic toxicities of surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Exploiting molecular vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies that selectively target tumor cell vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependency, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and targeted therapy resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the inhibition of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe antibody-based strategies used to direct immune effector mechanisms or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads to surface-antigen-bearing tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune-mediated targeting
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and methods to harness the immune system through checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and adoptive CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, historical outcomes, and future directions in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the broader clinical landscape of cancer management by evaluating genomic stratification, survival trends, combination strategies, and future therapeutic dilemmas.
